questions.q: What does choosing a Databricks Runtime Version actually determine?
options: The entire software stack the cluster boots: a specific Spark version, the OS, and Databricks' own added libraries and optimizations
Only the pricing tier of the workspace
Only which programming languages are available in a notebook
Nothing meaningful — all runtime versions are functionally identical
questions.explain: It's not "just Spark" — it's Spark plus everything Databricks adds on top.

questions.q: How does the Databricks Runtime differ from plain, open-source Apache Spark?
options: It adds further optimizations, native connectors, security patches, and compatibility fixes on top of open-source Spark
It removes Catalyst optimizer entirely and replaces it with something else
It is completely unrelated to Apache Spark
There is no real difference; Databricks Runtime is exactly identical to open-source Spark
questions.explain: This is a real, meaningful part of why teams choose Databricks over running raw open-source Spark themselves.

questions.q: Why should a scheduled production job pin to a specific LTS runtime version?
options: So a routine platform upgrade elsewhere doesn't unexpectedly change behavior underneath a job nobody's actively watching
LTS versions are always faster than non-LTS versions
Non-LTS versions cannot run scheduled jobs at all
Pinning to LTS is required to use Photon
questions.explain: Interactive, exploratory work can more safely track the newest version instead, since a human is present to notice issues.

options: Much of the SQL and DataFrame work from Foundations' Chapter 4 — the same PySpark code runs unmodified, just faster
Only notebook rendering speed in the browser, not actual query execution
Only jobs running on job clusters, never all-purpose clusters
Network transfer speed between workspaces
questions.explain: Photon is a native, vectorized query engine that's been on by default since Databricks Runtime 9.1 LTS.

questions.q: When would you typically disable Photon?
options: Only for a specific, documented compatibility issue with something else you're running
Photon should always be disabled for production jobs
Photon must be disabled to use widgets
Photon only works with job clusters, so it's disabled by default on all-purpose clusters
questions.explain: It's been the default for years, since it accelerates the same code without requiring any changes to it.
